article.title: NFL EDGE Monday Morning Brief
article.dek: Monday night is the whole slate: the Bills-Rams injury report, both cards on Buffalo, and a quiet board around them.

items.headline: Monday night injury report: Bills down two starters, three game-time calls
paragraphs: The final injury reports are in for tonight's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff at SoFi Stadium, and Buffalo is the banged-up side. The Bills ruled OUT defensive tackle Ed Oliver (knee) and wide receiver Joshua Palmer (shoulder) — Palmer got hurt in Friday's practice and the team is still running tests. Three more are questionable and will be game-time calls: wide receiver DJ Moore (shoulder), cornerback Dee Alford (ankle), and defensive lineman Landon Jackson (knee). Head coach Joe Brady said Moore, who was limited Saturday, will get the full 48 hours before a decision.

The counterweight for Buffalo: cornerback Christian Benford (toe) is 'good to go' after missing last week, and rookie receiver Skyler Bell will be active for his NFL debut with Palmer out. For the Rams, the only questionable tag is safety Quentin Lake (hip), and Sean McVay called it minor and expects him to play. Aaron Donald (back), Colby Parkinson, and Jaylen Watson are all good to go after missing time. Myles Garrett (knee, injured reserve) is progressing but the Rams are unlikely to open his practice window next week.

The official inactive lists land about 90 minutes before kickoff — that's when the Moore, Alford, Jackson, and Lake tags resolve. Until then, treat the questionable names as live uncertainty, not priced-in fact.
items.takeaway: Buffalo's receiver room is the swing factor — inactives resolve 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Quarterback check: the board matches the news
paragraphs: The app's quarterback feed is fresh this morning and matches the reporting. Josh Allen is Buffalo's expected starter, Matthew Stafford is the Rams' expected starter, and neither carries an injury flag on the board.
That's the check that matters on a game day morning: Stafford's back was last week's story and the Rams say he's good to go; the board agrees. No stale number to fade, no rumor to chase.
items.takeaway: Allen vs. Stafford, confirmed on both sides. Bet the game, not the rumor.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Hit Rate is on Buffalo — and it's a dog
paragraphs: Hit Rate means the supported pick the app thinks is most likely to win — win probability first, value second. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate. Tonight it's Buffalo on the moneyline at +150 on DraftKings, visiting the Rams at 8:15 p.m. ET.

The honest number: the app evaluates Buffalo's chance at 37.2% against a 40.0% breakeven at +150 — just short, reliability MEDIUM. The model's raw read likes Buffalo better than the market does (it has the Bills about two points better than the spread implies), but liking a team and the price paying you are two different things. The card chases the win, not the value; tonight the win is a dog and the price barely misses.
If your book has Buffalo better than +150, that's a better number than the card; if it's worse, tap Check and run your price before you decide.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate chases the win, not the value. Tonight the win is a dog.

items.headline: Balanced stays with Buffalo; Value finds nothing
paragraphs: Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much, a good starting point for a new bettor. It's Buffalo +3.5 at -118 on DraftKings. The app's evaluated chance is 47.4% against a 54.1% breakeven — short, reliability MEDIUM.

Value is always the model's +EV play, and tonight the Value lane is empty again: no offer on the board satisfies the lane's contract. Some mornings the board's honest answer is nothing. That's the report, not a failure — a quiet board is information too.
items.takeaway: Two cards on Buffalo, both thin; the honest third card is empty.

items.headline: How to use this before kickoff
paragraphs: Every news item above closes the loop the same way. The board refreshes every morning and evening. When your book isn't DraftKings or FanDuel, or the line moved since the board last refreshed, tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet/no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.

One mechanics note: +150 means every $1 you risk wins $1.50; -118 means every $1.18 you risk wins $1. That's price mechanics, not a stake — the app sizes your actual stake from your bankroll and your staking setting, which is deliberately conservative.
items.takeaway: Report the news first, then use it: Check is how news becomes a number.

items.headline: Learn the Game: key numbers
paragraphs: Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: imagine a team is favored by 3.5 points. In the NFL, games land on a 3-point margin more than any other number — field goals are the unit of the sport. That's why 3 (and 7) are called key numbers: the most common final margins, and the numbers every spread is measured against.

When a spread crosses a key number — say from -3 to -3.5 — the favorite now has to win by more than a field goal instead of exactly one. That half-point is a bigger ask than it looks, which is why books charge heavier juice around key numbers. Watching where a line sits relative to 3 and 7 tells you more than watching whether it moved a point.

Our Fade rule needs a verified public-vs-sharper split plus corroboration before it becomes a play. I checked the free VSiN splits row this morning: it showed Sunday's already-played Eagles-Jaguars game, not tonight's, so no split qualified. When a real one does, this section will say so plainly.
items.takeaway: The half-point that crosses a key number is worth more than any other half-point — price it like it matters.

items.headline: Buffalo's price barely moved — 3.5 stands
paragraphs: Overnight the Monday-night number did almost nothing. DraftKings had Buffalo +3.5 at -115 last evening; this morning it's +3.5 at -118, and FanDuel matches at +3.5 -118. The moneyline is steady at Buffalo +150 on both books, and the DraftKings total sits at 54.5. The board caught it all — the market snapshot was fresh when we read it.

That's a juice nudge toward Buffalo, not a line move: 3.5 hasn't budged. One shopping note from the same board: Pinnacle is dealing Buffalo +162 on the moneyline, a better price than the +150 on DraftKings and FanDuel. If your book beats the card's number on either side, run it through Check — your price gets its own verdict.
items.takeaway: The line stood still; the juice leaned Buffalo. Shop the number.

items.headline: One game, one number, one Check
paragraphs: Tonight's prices: Buffalo +150 on the moneyline and +3.5 at -118 on the spread at DraftKings. The questionable tags — Moore, Alford, Jackson, Lake — resolve when inactives land about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. Until then, your book's line is the only line that matters — run it through Check.
And the occasional honest nudge: settlement is manual, no auto-settle. The tracker only works if you're honest with yourself — log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Check the price you can actually bet, then be honest about the result.
